**Finding: compliant (at fallback) — no redline proposed.**

Section 13 (continuing at p0090–p0093) does contain a Garman-side IP indemnity, notwithstanding that the opening paragraph is pure ownership language:

- **Vendor indemnity present:** Garman warrants it owns/controls all necessary rights and indemnifies and holds Sparkling (and its officers/directors) harmless from all Losses — court costs, settlement amounts, reasonable legal fees — arising from breach of that warranty.
- **Standard remedies:** procure the right, procure an equivalent element, or replace/modify (p0091–p0093).
- **Uncapped:** Section 15 states the liability limitation "shall not apply to breaches of Sections 13 and 14," so the indemnity is not subject to any cap — better than the fallback's 3× annual fees super-cap.
- **No one-way exposure:** there is no reciprocal Sparkling indemnity anywhere in the document.

Noted but not flagged (sub-elements short of preferred): no express duty to *defend*; no indemnity heads for Garman's breach of law, data breach, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; no refund remedy; and a tight ten-calendar-day notice window. If the negotiation reopens Section 13 for other reasons, these are worth folding in — particularly the duty to defend and the data-breach head — but individually they do not fail the fallback.
